free_tier.stated: Still trading, but the reason to record it is a data-loss incident rather than a price: several Los Angeles host nodes were compromised through a Virtualizor vulnerability, the boot sectors of affected guest disks were overwritten with a ransom note, and the vendor states that the data on those disks cannot be recovered. The vendor's own wording, reposted in the forum: 攻击者损坏了与VPS相关的磁盘，磁盘上的数据无法恢复.

egress.terms: The paid SSD VPS plans include 4 TB (SSD VPS 1) to 25 TB (SSD VPS 6) of bandwidth a month at 1 Gb/s; no overage price is published on the plan page.
egress.free_allowance: none free; 4 TB/Mo at 1 Gb/s included in the paid SSD VPS 1 plan
egress.price_per_tb: not published: the plan page states no overage price

interface_detail: REST API and SSH, per the CloudCone API page: "CloudCone REST API allows you to access most of the features available at app.cloudcone.com", and per the VPS page: "Use the recovery mode to gain direct access via SSH."
tooling: language bindings, per the CloudCone API page: "We have language bindings in some programming languages."
chaining: This is the reason any free or cheap host needs a second copy elsewhere: the composition that survives an incident is two providers plus an object store, not one provider plus its own snapshots.
limits_note: What fails is durability: a hypervisor-level compromise destroyed guest disks across several nodes and the vendor confirmed non-recovery, so a snapshot kept on the same provider is not a backup.
binding_note: What fails is durability: a hypervisor-level compromise destroyed guest disks across several nodes and the vendor confirmed non-recovery, so a snapshot kept on the same provider is not a backup.

identity_cost.detail: The signup route was not read; the record is about the incident, not the account door.

evidence.proved: the vendor letter is reposted: 我们使用的平台（Virtualizor）存在一个漏洞，攻击者获得了...节点的访问权限...磁盘上的数据无法恢复, quoted from the snippet
a write-up states the boot sector of affected virtual machines was overwritten with a ransom note and that recovery proceeded by inspecting raw block devices and rebuilding partition tables
a summary states CloudCone subsequently confirmed 数据已遭不可逆损毁 (the data was irreversibly destroyed) and that the ransom demand recovered nothing, quoted
SSD VPS 1 at '$2.33 /MO' with 'Billed $28 per year', 2 vCPU, 1 GB dedicated RAM, 30 GB SSD, 4 TB/Mo at 1 Gb/s, quoted from the plan card
